newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Lend Lease says on track for profits rise.
newsitem.headline: Lend Lease says on track for profits rise.

text.p: Lend Lease Corp, announcing its US$400 million acquisition of Equitable Real Estate Investment Management, said it was on target to increase profits and earnings per share (EPS) in the current financial year ending June 30.
The purchase would be funded through a mixture of debt, including a US$100 million note to Equitable, and existing cash reserves, Lend Lease Chairman Stuart Hornery said in a statement.
"For our shareholders, the acquisition will be earnings per share positive from the outset," he said.
Lend Lease chief executive David Higgins said Equitable Real Estate (ERE) managed about US$25 billion in property and mortgages for a large cross section of U.S. and international investors.
ERE was the largest manager of investment real estate in the United States.
"This will greatly strengthen our capacity to undertake outsourced facilities management on a global basis," Higgins said.

"In response to the rapidly increasing sophistication of the market, Lend Lease is now strategically placed to service a growing demand among institutional investors in the US for the complete spectrum of real estate investment advice, opportunities and services, both in the U.S. and around the world," he said.
ERE had posted earnings before tax and non-recurring items of US$56 million in calendar 1996, he said.
"In closing, Mr Higgins stated Lend Lease was on target to increase profits and earnings per share in the current financial year," Lend Lease said.
Lend Lease said in February it expected to increase profit after tax and EPS in the year to June 30, 1997 from its 1995/96 profit figure of A$280 million.
Lend Lease's shares were 32 cents higher at A$22.85 at 4.10 p.m. (0610 GMT) on Thursday.
